subject: Request: network tail-latency exclusion for Private deployment SLA - HorizonBio
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@horizonbio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment SLA - network tail latency discussion

Hi Asha,

Thanks for the call earlier — appreciate the deep dive on HorizonBio's WAN topology. As discussed, HorizonBio will run Redwood Private in a colo at your primary site and route traffic across your internal load balancers and WAN links to the compute cluster. Given the amount of cross-datacenter hops and some persistent packet loss spikes you've seen, you asked whether we can exclude network tail latency that is under customer control from the end-to-end 99.9% latency SLO in the contract.

To move this forward I captured the ask and a proposed scope:
- Exclusion scope: downstream network events under HorizonBio control (internal LB failures, on-prem WAN link degradations, customer-managed firewall queuing)
- Proposed metric: Redwood will measure server-side processing latency; any end-to-end requests where packet loss/reordering is detected by your netops as the primary root cause will be classified as customer-network events and excluded from SLA calculation.
- Evidence: customer to provide NetFlow/packet captures or the network diagnostic logs (sample attached).
- Implementation: tech integration between our tracer and your netops alerts (we can send a webhook or you can push syslogs)

Next steps: can you confirm acceptance of the scope above and share the NetOps contact and any SLAs you require for exclusion confirmation turn-around (e.g., 48 hours to validate events)? Once we have that I'll draft an explicit contract amendment for legal.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: HorizonBio_network-diagnostic-log-20280530.txt (log excerpt)

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@horizonbio.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: HorizonBio Networking Team <netops@horizonbio.com>
Date: 2028-06-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA - network tail latency discussion

Rishi — thanks, this captures the ask. A few clarifications from our side: we can provide flow logs and pcap snippets for specific incidents; however we do not want continuous packet capture forwarded to third parties. We need a 72-hour window to validate suspected network events (busy schedule for NetOps). Also, our security/compliance team requires that any exclusion not broaden "availability" obligations — i.e. Redwood still needs to maintain control-plane availability.

From a contractual point of view we can accept exclusions when:
1) Our NetOps concurs that the primary root cause is customer-network and provides the event evidence; and
2) Redwood’s server-side logs show no processing or queuing anomalies on your end.

If Redwood can add a clear mutually agreeable process (ticketing + evidence exchange + 72h validation), we are comfortable with an exclusion limited to network-tail incidents. Please route the draft amendment to your legal contact.

—Asha
Director, IT Infrastructure
HorizonBio

(Attachment: none)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@horizonbio.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-03T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA - network tail latency discussion

Asha — looping in Markus from Legal for the formal amendment. Rishi and I reviewed the operational proposal and have an internal redline ready. Quick summary of changes we'll propose in the amendment (attached as PDF):

- Definition: "Customer Network Event" will be narrowly defined (list of event types + required evidence).
- Evidence exchange: HorizonBio provides NetOps confirmation + sample pcap/flow snippet; Redwood provides server-side traces and tokenized request IDs.
- Validation period: 72 hours from event ticket creation for initial validation (per your ask).
- Control plane carve: Redwood will maintain the control-plane uptime SLA for management endpoints; exclusion applies only to data-plane latency in scope.
- Audit: Both parties agree to an annual audit of exclusion usage, capped at 12 incidents/year before a contract review is triggered.

Two asks from our side: 1) we need a named NetOps contact who can sign off on evidence within 72 hours; 2) please confirm you are comfortable with the audit cap (12 incidents). If you confirm, Markus will produce a short amendment and we can attach the SLA redlines to the Master Services Agreement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_draft_redlines.pdf

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@horizonbio.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, HorizonBio Networking Team <netops@horizonbio.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA - network tail latency discussion

Marissa, Markus — thanks for the clear summary. HorizonBio accepts the proposed structure with two small modifications:
- Validation window: we can commit to the 72-hour validation but request an initial 5-business-day period for the first quarter after go-live to avoid false positives while our monitoring baselines stabilize.
- Audit cap: increase to 18 incidents/year for the first 12 months, then revert to 12 unless both parties agree otherwise.

NetOps contact: Ravi Menon (ravi.menon@horizonbio.com) will be primary. Ravi is also copied on this thread. He will triage tickets and provide evidence.

Please send the amendment with those two changes and we'll have Legal review.

—Asha

(Attachment: none)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@horizonbio.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@horizonbio.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA - network tail latency discussion

Asha / Ravi — appreciate the flexibility. We'll incorporate the two items into the amendment:
1) 72-hour validation window as the steady-state process, plus an initial 5-business-day stabilization window post go-live (explicitly timeboxed for 90 days).
2) Audit cap set to 18 incidents/year for first 12 months, then 12 thereafter unless mutually changed.

We will prepare and circulate the "SLA Amendment — Network Tail Exclusion" draft today. Expected turn-around: legal redline back to you within 3 business days.

Operational notes for Rishi/Marissa: please confirm webhook vs syslog option with Ravi and include sample tokenized traces when we send the draft.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_sla_response_v1.pdf
